records.issue_text: absolutize_urls only rewrites href/src starting with '/' and doesn't sanitize javascript: or other unsafe schemes; combined with raw_html cook_method rendered unsanitized via raw post.cooked, this allows stored XSS from RSS feeds or embedded remote content
records.rationale: The diff shows Post#cook returns `raw` unmodified for cook_method raw_html, and the embed view renders `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. TopicEmbed#import takes RSS content and embeds URLs without sanitizing href/src schemes (absolutize_urls only handles leading '/'), so a malicious feed or remote page could inject javascript: URLs or unsafe HTML that renders unsanitized. This is a verifiable stored XSS vector introduced by the diff.

records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb can set url to a non-URL feed GUID when blank or not matching http(s) pattern, which later causes URI(url) to raise an uncaught URI::InvalidURIError in absolutize_urls, breaking the whole feed poll for one bad item
records.rationale: The mechanism is verifiable in the diff: poll_feed.rb sets `url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//` with no validation that i.id is a URI, and TopicEmbed.import's guard `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` only filters before absolutize_urls — actually that guard would block non-URLs. However URI(url) in absolutize_urls can still raise URI::InvalidURIError for malformed http URLs with bad characters (e.g. spaces), and the guard regex passes them. Plausible uncaught exception breaking the hourly poll; partially mitigated by the regex guard, so confidence moderate.
